name: Sensor alarm windows
brief:
A server-room sensor raises an alarm for every run of `k` consecutive readings whose average is at least `t`. The input comes as one string:

- the first line holds `n`, `k` and `t`, separated by spaces;
- the second line holds the `n` readings, whole numbers separated by spaces (it may be missing when `n` is 0).

Write `solve_sensor_alarm(text)`, which returns, as a string, how many of the windows of `k` consecutive readings have an average of at least `t`. When `k` is larger than `n` there are no windows. Expect extra spaces and a trailing newline.

Example. For `"6 3 5\n4 6 5 2 9 7\n"` the window sums are 15, 13, 16 and 18, against a bar of 15. So the answer is `"3"`.
constraints: $0 \le n \le 200{,}000$, $1 \le k \le 200{,}000$, readings and $t$ whole numbers between $-10^6$ and $10^6$.
$O(n)$ time after reading is the target. Summing each window afresh is too slow when `k` is large.
Each test has its own 5-second limit in the browser.
hint: Compare the window sum with `k * t` instead of dividing, so no rounding creeps in. Slide the sum as each new reading arrives.

examples.note: Windows summing to 15, 16 and 18 reach the bar of 15; the one summing to 13 does not.
Two readings cannot fill a window of three, so there is no alarm.

how: Submit runs 12 hidden tests. Each answer must equal the expected value.
notes: A fixed window keeps a running sum: one reading in, one reading out.
The average must be at least `t`, so compare `sum >= k * t`; dividing whole numbers would round away a near miss.
